L29: # Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
L30: Matija Bucić ^{†}^{†}thanks: Faculty of Mathematics, University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria. This research was funded in whole or in part by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) 10.55776/AST2416125. Email: matija.bucic@univie.ac.at.    Fankang He ^{†}^{†}thanks: Faculty of Mathematics, University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria. Email: fankang.he@univie.ac.at.
L31:    Hyunwoo Lee ^{†}^{†}thanks: Department of Mathematical Sciences, KAIST, South Korea and Extremal Combinatorics and Probability Group (ECOPRO), Institute for Basic Science (IBS). E-mail: hyunwoo.lee@kaist.ac.kr. Supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea government(MSIT) No. RS-2023-00210430, and the Institute for Basic Science (IBS-R029-C4).
L32: ###### Abstract
L33: 
L34: In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any $n\geq k-1\geq 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_{k}^{n}$ for some $c_{k}<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k\geq 3$.
L35: ## 1 Introduction
L36: A collection of distinct sets is said to be a sunflower if all their pairwise intersections are the same set. Sunflowers provide a simple way to separate the common structure of several sets from the parts that do not interact. This makes them useful both for finding order in large families and for simplifying collections of combinatorial witnesses. They are part of a basic toolkit in extremal combinatorics and Ramsey theory, with countless applications.
L37: They are also a tool for proving lower bounds for monotone circuits deciding whether a graph has a clique of specified size or a perfect matching and for studying thresholds of monotone properties [【16†2】, 【17†50】]. In additive combinatorics, they are connected to the cap-set problem, while their vector and multicolored versions underpin combinatorial approaches to fast matrix multiplication [【16†2】, 【18†7】].
L38: They also underlie the compression of the hitting set instances in parameterized algorithms [【19†5】], while information theory supplies a useful tool for arguing about sunflowers through Shannon’s noiseless coding theorem; see [【20†49】].
L39: Many of the above connections are underpinned by natural extremal questions concerning sunflower-free families. The most famous of these are arguably the Erdős-Rado sunflower conjecture [【21†20】] and the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture [【22†22】, 【23†25】, 【24†21】]. The latter is concerned with the very natural question of how large can the family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ be if it does not contain a sunflower consisting of $k$ sets?
L40: This question has been repeated many times over the years, with the oldest reference the authors could find dating back to 1970, both by Erdős with various coauthors [【22†22】, 【25†23】, 【23†25】, 【26†24】, 【27†26】, 【28†28】, 【29†29】, 【30†30】, 【24†21】], and by other authors [【31†18】, 【32†13】, 【33†14】, 【34†41】, 【16†2】, 【18†7】, 【35†44】, 【36†35】, 【37†34】, 【38†43】, 【39†32】, 【40†4】, 【41†1】, 【42†45】, 【43†31】, 【44†16】, 【45†52】, 【46†47】, 【47†42】, 【48†9】].
L41: Erdős and Szemerédi [【24†21】], proved that for any fixed $k\geq 3$ the answer is at most $2^{n-\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ and conjectured that the answer should be exponentially smaller than $2^{n}$. Using improved uniform sunflower bounds of Kostochka [【49†40】], Deuber, Erdős, Gunderson, Kostochka, and Meyer [【31†18】] strengthened this to $2^{n-\sqrt{n\log\log n}/{\log\log\log n}}$ for large $n$.
L42: The breakthrough on the uniform problem due to Alweiss, Lovett, Wu, and Zhang [【40†4】], from 2019, improved the bound to $2^{n-n/(\log n)^{1+o(1)}}$. Subsequent refinements [【20†49】, 【50†6】] (in particular the one due to Rao [【20†49】]) give a slightly sharper bound of $2^{n-\Omega(n/\log n)}$, see [【40†4】, Theorem 4.1].
L43: For the special case of $k=3$, an important connection to additive combinatorics was established by Alon, Shpilka, and Umans [【16†2】], who showed that an exponential improvement over the trivial bound for cap sets in $\mathbb{F}_{3}^{n}$ would imply the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture in the $k=3$ case. Here, the polynomial-method breakthroughs of Croot, Lev, and Pach [【51†15】] and Ellenberg and Gijswijt [【52†19】] in 2016 supplied this cap-set estimate.
L44: Naslund and Sawin [【35†44】] then gave a direct argument giving the base of the exponent of ${3}/{2^{2/3}}\approx 1.89$ in the upper bound. Their proof, using Tao’s slice-rank formulation of the polynomial method [【53†53】], turns the absence of a sunflower into a diagonal tensor. The slice rank of that tensor measures the size of the family, while an expansion of its coordinatewise definition gives an upper bound.
L45: The same circle of ideas connects cap sets, tensors, and the group-theoretic approach to matrix multiplication [【18†7】].
L46: We prove the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture for every $k\geq 3$.
L47: ###### Theorem 1.
L48: 
L49: For every integer $k\geq 3$ and every integer $n\geq 1$, any subset of $2^{[n]}$ not containing a sunflower consisting of $k$ sets has size at most
L50: 
L51:  | $$3\left(2-\frac{1}{16k^{3}}\right)^{n}.$$  |

L27: #### Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
L28: 
L29: 【15†Image: Contact】
L30: 
L31: 【16†Image: Add Comment】
L32: 
L33: 【17†TR26-220】 Authors: 【18†Bruno Pasqualotto Cavalar】, 【19†Théo Fabris】, 【20†Partha Mukhopadhyay】, 【21†Srikanth Srinivasan】, 【22†Amir Yehudayoff】
L34: Publication: 28th September 2026 18:10
L35: Downloads: 577
L36: 
L37: Keywords:
L38: 
L39: 【23†Derandomization of Robust Sunflower lemmas】, 【24†Monotone Arithmetic Circuits】, 【25†monotone Boolean circuits】, 【26†Nisan-Wigderson designs】, 【27†the method of moments】
L40: 
L41: Abstract:
L42: Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d.
L43: distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution.
L44: We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable.
L45: Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest.
L46: We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an \emph{explicit} family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of \emph{sub-exponential} size.
L47: This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.
